A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SELF-PARAM and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original content can be matched reliably despite the revised title and expanded later version.

before.justification: v1 reports original context-injection and conversational-recommendation experiments in Tables 1–3 and sequential-retention results in Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds generator, diversity, regularization, and sequential fine-tuning comparisons in Section 4.5 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The procedure still matches contextual and context-free model predictions using KL divergence, generated QA pairs, and unrelated SlimPajama sentences. Testing alternative QA-generator checkpoints is an experimental variation, not a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use PwC for single, batch, and sequential context injection, INSPIRED and REDIAL for conversational recommendation, and SlimPajama for regularization. The added ablations reuse this coverage without introducing another task or domain.

E2.justification: Appendix B.2 adds FT (C) and FT (S) comparisons to sequential injection, where v1 reported SELF-PARAM against its uninjected starting performance. Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged; conversational FT (Q) is merely renamed FT (S).

E3.justification: New ablations vary the QA generator, compare 50 QA pairs for one epoch against 10 pairs for five epochs, and introduce sequential regularization and fine-tuning controls. Original splits and metrics remain. Table 6's one-epoch description conflicts with the retained 50-epoch batch setting in Appendix A.2, so it does not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix B add substantive tests of dependence on GPT-4o-mini, QA diversity, SlimPajama regularization, and sequential fine-tuning alternatives. These investigate sources of efficacy and retention that v1 did not isolate. The training-objective discussion reuses Tables 1–3 and is not itself new experimental evidence.

E5.justification: The original 50-sequence averaging remains unchanged. Appendix B.2 adds replication information stating 25 sequences for the new context-fine-tuning control, although its figure caption states 50. This is limited, internally inconsistent reporting; neither an increased run count nor new confidence intervals, seed disclosures, or significance tests is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figure 2 retain their numerical results, but Tables 4 and 6 and Figures 3–5 add substantial diagnostic findings. For example, Table 4 reports Mistral-7B batch QA-F1 of 0.4836 using its instruct counterpart versus 0.4384 using GPT-4o-mini at 500 contexts. These are results under different generator settings, not a same-setting improvement between versions.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly writes prompt conditioning in Equation 2 and absorbs the prompt into the sentence in Equation 3, using expectation notation. This restates the conditional-matching rationale already present in v1's Figure 1 caption and its KL objective. No substantive new formal assumption, theorem, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of effective context integration, long-term retention, superiority to existing methods, and no additional storage parameters. The revised title and added supporting experiments do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of approximately doubled computational cost and hallucination risks. It interprets the new controls as showing that stronger QA generators are unnecessary, diversity matters, and SlimPajama preserves injection functionality. Appendix B.2 also acknowledges comparable retention for FT (S), while distinguishing its lower immediate efficacy.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, alternative generator checkpoint names, newly described filtering of context-dependent questions, and implementation information for the new ablations. The hardware, learning rate, LoRA configuration, and generation prompt in Appendix A are retained. The reproducibility statement mainly points to existing sections.

R1.justification: v2 adds retrieval references by Izacard et al. and Wang et al. (2022), removes the knowledge-washing and multimodal references, and explicitly distinguishes its approach from stronger-teacher distillation in Section 4.5. The overall research positioning remains intact; the MemoryLLM publication update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: The title and publication header change, FT (Q) terminology is standardized, and discussion, ablation, ethics, reproducibility, and appendix sections are added. Most existing prose and the main narrative order remain intact, so this is an expansion rather than extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with two ablation tables and three sequential-injection heatmaps. Figure 1 corrects the prompt/context labels, including the updated model's input. Existing displays are retained and repositioned, and the recommendation-metric summary moves from Table 4 to Table 5.

improvement.justification: The generator and regularization controls address previously untested explanations for SELF-PARAM's performance, while the cost discussion and code-access information improve transparency. However, conflicting epoch counts, 25-versus-50 sequence descriptions, and reversed Figure 4/5 references weaken the new appendix evidence. The useful additional support therefore yields a limited net improvement rather than a clearly substantial one.
